correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3, real nonzero J, and strictly positive on-site reaction rates, the finite-dimensional maximal H-invariant kernel of Q is the permanent-survival subspace. Fourier total-momentum sectors diagonalize H. For nonflat sectors the only frequency collisions are exchange pairs; for even n the k=n/2 flat sector contributes exactly one bright diagonal vector. Counting exchange fixed points proves the dimensions. The exact diagonal entry of the bright projector gives the antipodal and n mod 4 branches. Independently diagonalized finite models n=3..10 corroborate all 380 ordered site probabilities, 328 bosonic probabilities and 24 lossy evolutions; finite tests are not used as a proof of n-uniform results.

value.rationale: Coincidence loss is an intrinsic quantum-reaction observable; the theorem supplies complete exact absorption probabilities on the natural infinite family of cyclic networks, uniformly over site-varying reaction strengths. It exposes the physically nontrivial contrast: no symmetric dark states for odd n versus many symmetric protected states for even n, with a quantitatively distinct antipodal configuration depending on n mod4. This is more than a renaming of antisymmetry or a small numerical special case. Its scope excludes interacting, flux-threaded, and disordered rings and finite-time kinetics.
